newsitem.title: USA: Key Democrat sees no need for power markets bill.
newsitem.headline: Key Democrat sees no need for power markets bill.

text.p: The top Democrat on the House Commerce Committee on Tuesday said he saw no need yet for Congress to require states to open their power markets to competition.

"I have doubts about the need for the Congress to impose its will upon the states, and concerns about whether the Congress has the depth of understanding and the vision (as) to where it wants to go at this particular point," said Rep. John Dingell of Michigan.

"I also have grave doubts as to whether there is sufficient consensus on this particular matter to enable us to legislate wisely," he told energy industry lobbyists at a National Energy Resources Organization luncheon.

Commerce Committee chairman Thomas Bliley, a Virginia Republican, and energy and power subcommittee chairman Dan Schaefer, a Colorado Republican, are currently pushing to pass a deregulation bill in the House this year.

"I have not reached a definitive conclusion about the merits of ... the various bills or the overall question of the principle, nor do I see a quick or easy solution to the enormously complex issues involved," Dingell said.

Based on responses he had received to 134 letters sent to utilities, state commissions, federal power marketing agencies, consumer advocates and others, Dingell said he was struck by the "enormous divergence of views."

"While few correspondents came out wholly against the idea of competition, quite a few were of the view that consumers would only benefit if local concerns and conditions were taken into account," he said.
"I want to see to it that we have enquired fully into that question before we move forward at the federal level," he said.
His comments underscored how difficult it would be for the House to pass a bill this year to restructure the electric industry.
